questions.question: If a school bus needs to be evacuated, passengers should:

options.text: Always use the rear door.
Always use the windows.
Always use the front door.
Use the safest exit.

questions.explanation: During an emergency evacuation, the driver must quickly decide which exit is safest. The driver then directs all students to that exit.

questions.question: Loading a school bus:

options.text: Is not a dangerous process.
Does not need to be supervised.
Should be done quickly.
Can be dangerous.

questions.explanation: More students are hurt or killed during loading and unloading than while riding the bus. Drivers must follow safety procedures during these times.

questions.question: Crossover mirrors help the driver see:

options.text: The danger zones in front of the bus.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The danger zones in front of the bus.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors show the danger zone directly in front of the bus. They also show danger zones on the left and right sides, from the front to the service door.

questions.question: If asked to back your vehicle into an alley, you should first:

options.text: Pull directly into the alley parking space.
Turn your vehicle right to face the alley.
Pull past the alley and stop perpendicular to it.
Pull past the alley and stop parallel to it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull past the alley and stop parallel to it.
questions.explanation: First, drive past the alley and stop parallel to it. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley. Your vehicle should fit completely within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: When entering an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Check for traffic.
Not use signals.
Abruptly enter a lane of traffic.
Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: Before entering an expressway, check traffic, use your signal, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: When checking air and electrical lines, all of the following should be true, except:

options.text: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
The air hoses and electrical lines are not cut.
The air lines are not pinched.
The air lines are not dragging on tractor parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: The air hoses are making a hissing noise.
questions.explanation: When inspecting air and electrical lines, listen for leaks. Check that lines are not cut, worn, tangled, pinched, or dragging on parts.

questions.question: Blind spots exist ____ the left and right side flat mirrors.

options.text: Immediately below
In the middle of
Above
To the left of

questions.explanation: Blind spots are located immediately below and in front of each outside flat mirror. Another blind spot exists directly behind the rear bumper.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no traffic control devices, the decision to proceed:

options.text: Rests with the driver.
Is indicated by a control device.
Is decided by the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: At passive railroad crossings (with no traffic control devices), the driver alone decides whether it is safe to cross the tracks.

questions.question: If exiting a bus during the vehicle control skills test, you must:

options.text: Keep both hands on the handrail.
Not touch the handrail.
Hold the handrail firmly.
Rush down the stairs.

questions.explanation: When exiting a bus, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. Hold the handrail firmly. Improper exiting results in automatic test failure.

questions.question: When doing a parallel parking maneuver, you should:

options.text: Back up past the parking space, then pull forward into it.
Drive forward past the parking space, then back into it.
Pull forward directly into the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive forward past the parking space, then back into it.
questions.explanation: Drive past the parking space on your right. Then back your vehicle into it, getting the rear as close to the back of the space as possible. Your vehicle must fit completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: How should you do pre-trip inspections?

options.text: Different each time to check different parts.
The same way every time so you don't forget anything.
Once in a while.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way every time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do your pre-trip inspection the same way before every drive. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you check everything.

questions.question: When a bus driver stops to pick up students, what should they do?

options.text: Put the vehicle in park.
Put the vehicle in first gear.
Put the vehicle in reverse.
Put the vehicle in third gear.

questions.explanation: When picking up students, put the school bus in park. If there is no park gear, put it in neutral instead.

questions.question: How should backing a school bus be treated?

options.text: It is strongly encouraged.
It is strongly discouraged.
It should only happen in the morning.

questions.explanation: Backing a school bus is strongly discouraged. Only do it if there is no other safe choice. If you must back up, follow all safety rules.

questions.question: When the examiner asks you to turn during the driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Don't use a turn signal because you were told to turn.
Only check traffic to your right.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.explanation: When asked to turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle be at the end of a basic vehicle control skills test exercise?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact spot the examiner described.
Within three feet of where the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact spot the examiner described.
questions.explanation: Park your vehicle in the exact position the examiner said. If you don't complete the exercise exactly as described, you may fail the basic control skills test.

questions.question: What does ABS allow a driver to do?

options.text: Drive faster.
Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
See farther ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep control of the vehicle while braking.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) prevents the wheels from locking up. It helps you keep control of your vehicle when braking on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: During the driving test, you will be checked on how you use your lane. Which is an example of poor lane use?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks.
Stopping behind crosswalks.
Driving in the left lane when more than one lane is available.
Finishing a right turn in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the left lane when more than one lane is available.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, don't drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines and crosswalks. On roads with multiple lanes, complete turns in the correct lane. Stay in or move to the right lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: During testing exercises (except straight line backing), how many times can you get out to check your vehicle's position?

options.text: One time.
Two times.
Three times.

questions.explanation: You can get out to check your vehicle's position during basic control skills tests. For straight line backing, you can only check once. For other exercises, you can check up to two times.

questions.question: After driving under an overpass during the driving test, what might the examiner ask you to remember?

options.text: The posted clearance height.
The posted weight limit.
The width of the opening.
If there was a shoulder near the road.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, if you pass under an overpass, the examiner may ask you to recall the posted clearance height.

questions.question: After driving over a bridge during the driving test, what might the examiner ask you to remember?

options.text: The posted weight limit.
The color of a sign you passed.
How many traffic lanes were on the bridge.
If there was a crosswalk on the bridge.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, if you cross a bridge, the examiner may ask you to recall the posted weight limit.
